title: Affine comparison of completed coherent arrows with adic module maps
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, C its positive-power coherent completion functor [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and h an additivity witness [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Let U be an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with its Noetherian open subscheme. Let rho be a zero-preserving restriction functor from coherent formal modules on X to those on U whose composite with the full inverse-system inclusion equals termwise open restriction [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness]. Given a short exact coherent complex S [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], put V = rho(C(S)). There exist a Noetherian commutative ring A [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], an ideal J of A, a short exact complex M of A-modules with finite middle term, and a zero-preserving functor F from coherent formal modules on U to A-modules which reflects limits of parallel pairs. There are A-linear equivalences $e_i:F(V_i)\simeq M_i^\wedge$ for $i=1,2,3$, where the completion is J-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], satisfying $e_2(F(V.f)(x))=\widehat{M.f}(e_1(x))$ and $e_3(F(V.g)(y))=\widehat{M.g}(e_2(y))$ for every x and y in the respective source modules. No injectivity or middle exactness of the completed maps is part of this conclusion.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0881 (lemma-exact), affine identification in the proof, and Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine)

proof.text: Take A to be the ring of sections of the affine open U, and J the sections of the restricted quasi-coherent ideal. The ring is Noetherian. The coherent inclusion preserves kernels and cokernels. Restriction to an open is sectionwise on its open site, preserves kernels and is a left adjoint, hence preserves cokernels. Affine sections of the restricted coherent sequence form a short exact complex M; its middle term is finite by coherence and the affine finite-type criterion.

Use the canonical affine isomorphism U ≅ Spec A to transport formal systems. The restricted ideal becomes the ideal sheaf associated to J by the tilde-sections adjunction. Apply the affine formal-module equivalence E. Compose E.functor with the full finite-module inclusion and scalar restriction from the completion to A, obtaining F. Naturality of E's limit cones implies preservation of zero. The equivalence and full inclusion reflect limits by full faithfulness. Scalar restriction preserves limits and reflects isomorphisms (ModuleCat.restrictScalars); since the completed ModuleCat has limits, reflectsLimitsOfShape_of_reflectsIsomorphisms gives its reflection of parallel-pair limits. Reflection is stable under composition.

Open restriction identifies products by I and, inductively, by its positive powers with the products by the restricted ideal powers; it preserves their quotient cokernels. The affine quotient and ideal-power formulas identify sections with M_i/J^(n+1)M_i and their arrows with reductions of M.f and M.g. The equality hρ identifies these systems with V after the formal-system inclusion.

The specified natural limit cones of E identify F.obj V.X_i with the inverse limits of the positive-power quotients of M_i. The inverse-limit definition of AdicCompletion uses also the initial zero quotient; adjoining or deleting that coordinate does not change the limit. Uniqueness of the limit comparison supplies the three A-linear equivalences e_i. On each quotient projection the induced completion map equals the reduction of the original map. Naturality of the cones and their jointly monomorphic projections give the displayed two equations.

lean.statement:
theorem formalCompletion_affine_comparison (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (h : (completion X I).Additive)
    (U : X.Opens) [IsNoetherian U.toScheme] (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (ρ : CoherentFormalModule X I ⥤ CoherentFormalModule U.toScheme (I.comap U.ι))
    (hz : ρ.PreservesZeroMorphisms)
    (hρ : ρ ⋙ (IsCoherentFormalModule (I.comap U.ι)).ι =
      (IsCoherentFormalModule I).ι ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ X.Modules U.toScheme.Modules).obj
          (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι))
    (S : ShortComplex (CoherentModules X)) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    let T := @ShortComplex.map _ _ _ _ _ _ S (completion X I)
      (@Functor.preservesZeroMorphisms_of_additive _ _ _ _ _ _ (completion X I) h)
    let V := @ShortComplex.map _ _ _ _ _ _ T ρ hz
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (_ : IsNoetherianRing A) (J : Ideal A)
      (M : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A)),
      Module.Finite A M.X₂ ∧ M.ShortExact ∧
      ∃ F : CoherentFormalModule U.toScheme (I.comap U.ι) ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A,
        F.PreservesZeroMorphisms ∧ ReflectsLimitsOfShape WalkingParallelPair F ∧
        ∃ (e₁ : F.obj V.X₁ ≃ₗ[A] AdicCompletion J M.X₁)
          (e₂ : F.obj V.X₂ ≃ₗ[A] AdicCompletion J M.X₂)
          (e₃ : F.obj V.X₃ ≃ₗ[A] AdicCompletion J M.X₃),
          (∀ x, e₂ ((F.map V.f) x) = AdicCompletion.map J M.f.hom (e₁ x)) ∧
          (∀ x, e₃ ((F.map V.g) x) = AdicCompletion.map J M.g.hom (e₂ x))
